note: Gold-standard set. Each case has two candidate boards. The one A.J. picks becomes the reference for that case; the comments say why, which is the part that generalises.

cases.name: Out the door in four minutes
cases.tests: The canonical case. Whether the reward the parent names is the reward that fits the window.

profile.sensoryNotes: Covers ears for loud noises; dislikes seamed socks

request.goal: Shoes on and in the car without a fight
request.obstacle: Every school morning we are fine until shoes. In four minutes they need shoes on with their go-bag and they need to be in the car. Shoes is where it stops.

tries.design: Takes the parent's own reward at face value. Two cards, no theme, swing in the garden before the car.
tries.title: First shoes, then swing

cards.label: Shoes
cards.imagePrompt: Flat vector icon, plain white background, no detail: a pair of children's sneakers

cards.label: Swing
cards.imagePrompt: Flat vector icon, plain white background, no detail: a garden swing seat on two ropes
cards.altText: A swing hanging from two ropes

plan.placement: Inside the front door, at Sam's eye level.
plan.reinforcement: Two minutes on the garden swing, before the car. Do not substitute.
plan.ifChallengingBehavior: Keep pointing at the FIRST card. Add no new words. Then still give the swing.
plan.generalization: The same two cards go in the go-bag for grandma's.

promptHierarchy.instruction: Point to the FIRST card. Say nothing.
Hold the shoes out at waist height.
Guide one foot in briefly, then let go.

tries.design: Moves the reward into the car so it survives a four-minute window, and themes it as a train line. Bets that a reward the parent cannot deliver is worse than a smaller one they can.
tries.title: Sam's first stop
tries.theme: Train line: First stop, Next stop

cards.label: Shoes on
cards.imagePrompt: Flat vector icon, plain white background, no detail: a pair of children's sneakers

cards.label: Train song
cards.imagePrompt: Flat vector icon, plain white background, no detail: a train carriage with a music note beside it
cards.altText: A train with a music note

script.phrase: First stop shoes. Next stop train song.

plan.placement: Inside the front door at Sam's eye level, laid out left to right like a route map.
plan.reinforcement: Start the train song as the car door shuts. Every time, same song.
plan.ifChallengingBehavior: Point at the FIRST card and wait. Do not repeat the sentence. The song still plays afterwards.
plan.generalization: Same two cards, same song, for the childminder's car.

promptHierarchy.instruction: Point to the FIRST card. Say nothing.
Put the shoes on the floor in front of Sam.
Guide one foot in briefly, then let go.

cases.name: Teeth at bedtime
cases.tests: Motivation or sequencing. Whether a twenty-minute battle wants a reward or a breakdown of the task.

profile.sensoryNotes: Hates the taste of mint toothpaste

request.goal: Teeth brushed without a twenty-minute argument
request.obstacle: Teeth at bedtime is a twenty-minute battle. She will do everything else in the routine without complaint.

tries.design: Treats it as motivation. Two cards. Bets that she can already brush her teeth and simply will not.
tries.title: First teeth, then dinosaurs

cards.label: Brush teeth
cards.imagePrompt: Simple black line drawing, white background, no shading: a toothbrush with toothpaste on it
cards.altText: A toothbrush with a line of toothpaste

cards.label: Dinosaur book
cards.imagePrompt: Simple black line drawing, white background, no shading: an open book with a stegosaurus on the page
cards.altText: An open book showing a stegosaurus

plan.placement: Taped to the bathroom mirror at Mia's eye level.
plan.reinforcement: The dinosaur book, in bed, straight afterwards. It is not read on nights she skips teeth.
plan.ifChallengingBehavior: Point at the FIRST card and wait without talking. She has time. Being rushed is a trigger.
plan.generalization: Both cards travel in the overnight bag.

promptHierarchy.instruction: Put the toothbrush in her hand.
Brush your own teeth beside her.

tries.sensoryHandling: Plan notes: swap to a non-mint toothpaste before trying this board. Mint is named as aversive and no reward outranks a taste she cannot tolerate.

tries.design: Treats it as sequencing. Four steps so the end is visible from the start. Bets the battle is about not knowing when it stops.
tries.title: Mia's teeth steps

cards.label: Wet brush
cards.imagePrompt: Simple black line drawing, white background, no shading: a toothbrush under a running tap

cards.label: Add paste
cards.imagePrompt: Simple black line drawing, white background, no shading: a tube of toothpaste squeezing onto a brush
cards.altText: Toothpaste being squeezed onto a brush

cards.label: Brush teeth
cards.imagePrompt: Simple black line drawing, white background, no shading: a child brushing their teeth

cards.label: Rinse
cards.imagePrompt: Simple black line drawing, white background, no shading: a cup of water being tipped towards a mouth

plan.placement: A strip of four cards along the bathroom mirror, left to right, with Velcro so she moves each one to a DONE box.
plan.reinforcement: Moving the last card to DONE is the finish. The dinosaur book follows in bed.
plan.ifChallengingBehavior: Name only the current step. Do not mention the remaining ones.
plan.generalization: The same four steps work at her dad's house with the same cards.

promptHierarchy.instruction: Point to the next undone card.
Name the step in two words.
Do the step yourself alongside her.

tries.sensoryHandling: Plan notes: swap to a non-mint toothpaste before trying this board. Step 2 is the step that fails otherwise.

cases.name: Leaving the playground
cases.tests: Type choice under pressure. A First-Then is the default and may be the wrong default when the trigger note names the real cause.

profile.triggerNotes: Ending a preferred activity with no warning

request.goal: Leave the playground without going to the floor
request.obstacle: Getting him off the playground. He is happy, then I say time to go, then he is on the floor and I am carrying him to the car.

tries.design: Reads the trigger note literally. The problem is not motivation, it is the absence of a warning. Two parameter cards, no reward.
tries.title: Two more, then done

cards.label: Two more slides
cards.imagePrompt: Flat vector icon, plain white background, no detail: a playground slide with the numeral 2 beside it
cards.altText: A slide with the number two

cards.label: All done park
cards.imagePrompt: Flat vector icon, plain white background, no detail: an open palm held up, facing forward

plan.placement: Both cards on a key ring clipped to the pram or your belt, shown at the playground, not kept in a bag.
plan.reinforcement: There is no reward here. The predictability is the intervention. Show WAIT at two slides remaining, every single visit.
plan.ifChallengingBehavior: Hold up the STOP card and walk to the gate. Do not renegotiate the count. Next visit, the count still means the count.
plan.generalization: The same pair ends swimming and ends screen time.

promptHierarchy.instruction: Hold up the WAIT card where he can see it.
Hold up two fingers beside the card.
Offer a hand at the bottom of the slide.

tries.design: Reads it as motivation and uses the default type. First card is leaving, Then card is a digger reward in the car.
tries.title: First car, then digger

cards.label: Walk to car
cards.imagePrompt: Flat vector icon, plain white background, no detail: a pair of children's shoes with a short arrow beside them

cards.label: Digger video
cards.imagePrompt: Flat vector icon, plain white background, no detail: a yellow digger with its arm raised

plan.placement: Two cards on a key ring on your belt. Shown at the gate, not at the slide.
plan.reinforcement: The digger video starts once he is buckled. Two minutes, then it stops.
plan.ifChallengingBehavior: Point at the FIRST card. Keep walking towards the car. The video still plays once he is in.
plan.generalization: Works for leaving the supermarket with the same two cards.

promptHierarchy.instruction: Hold out your hand towards the gate.

cases.name: Loses the thread in the morning
cases.tests: Granularity. Six steps is complete and five is used. Where the line sits.

request.goal: Get through the morning without me in the room
request.obstacle: He gets up fine, then I find him on the floor with one sock on. If I am not in the room, nothing happens.

tries.design: Six steps, complete coverage, tap to check off. Bets that the whole morning on one strip is what replaces the parent standing there.

plan.placement: A vertical strip on his bedroom door with four stations and a slider.

plan.ifChallengingBehavior: Ask which stop he is at. Nothing else.
plan.generalization: Add a fifth stop only once four are automatic.

cases.name: Dentist next Tuesday
cases.tests: Social narrative voice. First person commits the child to behaviour; third person describes what will happen.

profile.sensoryNotes: Very sensitive to bright light and to strangers touching her face

request.obstacle: She has a dentist appointment next Tuesday. Last time she screamed in the waiting room and we left without being seen.

tries.design: First person, standard Social Story voice. Reads as hers. Risk: it states what she will do, which is a promise she may not keep.
tries.title: My dentist visit

plan.placement: Read as a six-page booklet at bedtime, starting tonight, once a night until Tuesday. Take it to the appointment.
plan.reinforcement: Reading it is not a task to be rewarded. Keep it short and stop when she stops.
plan.ifChallengingBehavior: Stop at the page she stops at. Read one page tomorrow, not six.
plan.generalization: The same six-page shape works for a haircut and for a blood test.

promptHierarchy.instruction: Point to the picture on the page.

narrativeText: On Tuesday I am going to the dentist.
I will sit in the waiting room with Mum.
The dentist has a big chair that goes back.
There is a bright light. I can close my eyes.
The dentist looks at my teeth with a little mirror.
Then we go home in the car.

tries.design: Third person, describing what will happen rather than what she will do. Nothing is promised on her behalf. Risk: less personal, may not land as hers.

cases.name: Asking for the tablet forty times
cases.tests: Boundary or contingency. A WAIT card states a rule; a First-Then makes the tablet earnable. Both are defensible and they teach different things.

profile.sensoryNotes: Looks for deep pressure when upset

request.goal: Stop the afternoon being one long negotiation
request.obstacle: He asks for the tablet about forty times between school and dinner. Saying not yet makes it worse.

tries.design: A boundary, not a bargain. One WAIT card plus a visual timer. Bets that the forty asks are a question with no visible answer, and that a reliable answer ends them.
tries.title: Tablet after dinner

cards.label: Tablet after dinner
cards.imagePrompt: Flat vector icon, plain white background, no detail: a tablet device beside a dinner plate
cards.altText: A tablet next to a dinner plate

plan.placement: On the fridge at Ben's eye level, with a sand timer or clock face beside it showing dinner time.
plan.reinforcement: The tablet appears the moment dinner ends, every day. The card is only true if that happens.
plan.ifChallengingBehavior: Point at the card. Say the same four words. Never add a reason, and never move the time.
plan.generalization: The same card format works for sweets and for the park.

promptHierarchy.instruction: Point at the card without speaking.
Say "After dinner." Same words every time.

tries.design: Makes the tablet the Then. Bets that an earnable tablet is better than a timed one because it gives him something to do with the wanting.
tries.title: First dinner, then tablet

cards.label: Eat dinner
cards.imagePrompt: Flat vector icon, plain white background, no detail: a dinner plate with a fork

cards.label: Tablet
cards.imagePrompt: Flat vector icon, plain white background, no detail: a tablet device

plan.placement: On the fridge at Ben's eye level, where he asks from.
plan.reinforcement: Twenty minutes of tablet straight after dinner. Set it before he starts, so ending it is already agreed.
plan.ifChallengingBehavior: Point at the FIRST card. Do not discuss how much dinner counts. The tablet still comes.
plan.generalization: The same pair works for homework and for the bath.

cases.name: Swimming was cancelled
cases.tests: The hardest abstraction, and a gap in the spec. Role Choice exists in the data model but no support type uses it. Picking B says the spec needs fixing.

profile.triggerNotes: Plans changing after she has been told they are happening

request.goal: Survive a cancellation without losing the whole day
request.obstacle: Swimming was cancelled on Saturday and the rest of the day was gone. She had already been told it was happening.

tries.design: Two cards: the change, then one pre-agreed replacement decided in advance on a calm day. Bets that a known substitute beats a choice made while upset.
tries.title: Plan changed

cards.label: Plan changed
cards.imagePrompt: Flat vector icon, plain white background, no detail: a calendar page with a diagonal line through one square

cards.label: Backup plan
cards.imagePrompt: Flat vector icon, plain white background, no detail: a cloud with a small sun emerging beside it
cards.altText: A cloud with a sun behind it

plan.placement: Both cards live on the kitchen calendar. The backup plan is written on the back of the second card, chosen by Rosa on a calm weekday.
plan.reinforcement: No reward. Naming the change out loud is the whole intervention. Deliver the backup plan the same day it is shown.
plan.ifChallengingBehavior: Show the OOPS card once and say the four words. Do not explain why swimming was cancelled. The explanation is for later.
plan.generalization: The same pair covers a cancelled visit, a closed shop, a broken lift.

promptHierarchy.instruction: Put the OOPS card on the calendar square.

tries.design: Three cards: the change, then two options she picks between. Bets that agency at the moment of loss is worth more than predictability. Uses role Choice, which no support type currently permits.
tries.title: Plan changed, you pick

cards.label: Plan changed
cards.imagePrompt: Flat vector icon, plain white background, no detail: a calendar page with a diagonal line through one square

cards.label: Baking
cards.imagePrompt: Flat vector icon, plain white background, no detail: a mixing bowl with a wooden spoon

cards.label: Bike ride
cards.imagePrompt: Flat vector icon, plain white background, no detail: a bicycle seen from the side

plan.placement: The OOPS card goes on the cancelled calendar square. The two choice cards go beside it, face up.
plan.reinforcement: Her pick happens that day, without renegotiation. Two options only — three is a decision, not a comfort.
plan.ifChallengingBehavior: Leave the two cards out and walk away. She can pick in an hour. Do not pick for her.
plan.generalization: Keep a set of four choice cards; put out two of them, never all four.

promptHierarchy.instruction: Lay the two choice cards side by side.

tries.specGap: Card.Role includes Choice but SPEC section 2 defines no choice-board support type, and ParameterCards is specified as Wait, Stop, Oops. Preferring B means either adding a fifth type or widening ParameterCards.

cases.name: Head-banging in the supermarket
cases.tests: The refusal path. Whether a referral should also offer something, or whether offering anything dilutes it.

request.obstacle: When it gets too much in the supermarket he hits his head with his hand, hard, and I do not know what to do.

tries.design: Refers, and still offers one safe thing to try meanwhile. Bets that a parent who gets nothing back stops using the tool, and that a leave-now card is genuinely useful.
tries.reason: You described Theo hitting his head hard enough to worry you, which is not something a picture board should be the answer to.
tries.guidance: Call the paediatrician or the team who did Theo's assessment this week and use the words you used here. If it happens and you cannot keep him safe, leave the trolley and go straight out.
tries.stillUseful: A single LEAVE NOW card on your keys, shown as you walk out. It does not address the head-hitting; it just makes going a plan instead of a retreat.
tries.whatItDoesNotDo: No board, no script, no reinforcement plan. The referral is the output.

tries.design: Refers and offers nothing. Bets that any attached suggestion reads as the real answer and gets tried instead of the phone call.
tries.reason: You described Theo hitting his head hard, and that needs a person, not a printable.
tries.guidance: Ring the paediatrician or Theo's assessment team this week and tell them exactly what you told me, including how often. Until you have spoken to them, shop without him if there is any way to do that.
tries.whatItDoesNotDo: Nothing is offered deliberately. Anything offered here would be the thing that gets tried.
